newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Soporcel says 1997 bad year for pulp.
newsitem.headline: Soporcel says 1997 bad year for pulp.

text.p: Portuguese pulp producer Soporcel-Sociedade Portuguesa de Celulose considers that 1997 will be a bad year for the pulp sector and a good year for paper, managing director Luis Deslandes said.
"1997 will be bad for the pulp sector and good for paper," he told reporters during the presentation of the company's 1996 results.
He said he expected continuing weakness in pulp prices and strength in paper prices this year.
"1997 will be sluggish for the pulp sector, with mediocre prices," Deslandes said.
"The paper sector will have good sales, good prices and a good margin," he said. "The average prices of pulp in 1997 will not exceed the average prices for 1996."
Soporcel converts about two thirds of its pulp production into paper.
In 1996 it produced 422,500 tonnes of pulp and 285,800 tonnes of paper, compared with 397,500 and 258,900 tonnes respectively in 1995.
Earlier, Soporcel announced a 1996 net profit of 0.3 billion escudos, down from 11.2 billion in 1995, and said the depressed pulp sector explained the sharp drop in profits.
